design.role: Road and gate watch for Welcome; notices arrivals, departures, road conditions, and expected caravan traffic
design.background: He keeps watch at the road into Welcome. The job is not to control who may leave, but to notice who passes, whether the road is behaving normally, and when expected travelers fail to appear. Years of routine have made him attentive to small absences: no wheel noise, no dust, no messenger coming ahead of a delayed caravan.
personality: more comfortable with signs and routines than speculation
speech_style: talks about what he can actually see or hear
becomes noticeably more precise rather than more emotional when concerned
gameplay_purposes: establish the road out of Welcome as a real boundary without implementing a gate system
give the player fieldwork that naturally exercises combat, pickup, investigation, and combat-plus-retrieval
provide a second perspective on the expected and delayed caravan
teach through useful village work rather than explicit tutorial dialogue
serve as a recurring edge-of-settlement interaction point
narrative_purposes: make departures and arrivals part of ordinary village life
foreshadow danger through missing routine rather than prophecy
support the theme that absence becomes meaningful because people notice who should have returned
show Welcome as connected to a larger world through one watched road
let the player's growing competence be acknowledged through increasingly demanding errands

relationships.notes: The inn often hears from arrivals after the watchman sees them on the road. They share practical information about travelers and caravan timing.
The watchman sometimes brings damaged road gear or small repairs to the workshop; their relationship is practical rather than close.

beats.title: First meeting

lines.text: Heading out, coming in, or just standing where everyone does both?

choices.text: Anything I should know about the road?

beats.notes: First meeting establishes the watchman's function without turning him into a gatekeeper or tutorial narrator.

beats.title: About the road

lines.text: Keep to the road. Shortcuts are mostly roads that haven't had enough funerals to earn a name yet.
And if you mean to be gone long, tell someone. Not for permission. So we know where to start looking.

beats.notes: Road-safety flavor only. No travel restriction or tracking mechanic is implied.

beats.title: Waiting for the caravan

lines.text: Always waiting for someone. Today it's a caravan.
Usually I hear the wagons before I see them.

beats.notes: Works even before the explicit expected-caravan fact becomes relevant.

beats.title: Caravan expected today

lines.text: Caravan's due today. Nothing unusual in that.
By afternoon, the road usually starts making noise before the village does.

beats.notes: Routine expectation. It should not read as obvious foreshadowing on first encounter.

beats.title: Caravan is late

lines.text: No dust. No bells. No runner ahead.
Could be a broken axle. Could be weather. I'd prefer one of those.

beats.notes: Concern is expressed through missing expected signs, not unexplained knowledge.

beats.title: Fieldwork 1 — clear the road

lines.text: I've got a small job if you're heading out.
Something's been nesting around the first road marker. Small, mean, and confident enough to chase people off the road.
Clear the ones holding the road. Don't follow them into the brush just to prove a point.

beats.notes: Combat-training job. Exact enemy definition and required count are intentionally not frozen here. Gameplay completion should set welcome.watch.road_pests.cleared=true through the authoritative gameplay owner.

beats.title: Fieldwork 1 — active reminder

lines.text: First marker past the gate. Clear the road, not the whole countryside.

beats.notes: Reminder only.

beats.title: Fieldwork 1 — road cleared

lines.text: Road's quiet again. Good.
You came back without chasing trouble farther than the job required. Better.

beats.notes: Acknowledges combat completion and deliberately rewards restraint as well as success.

beats.title: Fieldwork 2 — gather road-marker cloth

lines.text: Since you're already learning the road, there's another thing.
The wind tore marker cloth off the outer posts. Bring me a bundle's worth of the pieces you find along the road.
Bright cloth looks useless right up until fog decides otherwise.

beats.notes: Pickup/collection job. The authored hand-in uses one logical bundle item because NPC Lab currently models item possession as boolean, not a quantity condition. World collection/counting remains future gameplay work.

beats.title: Fieldwork 2 — active reminder

lines.text: Marker cloth tends to catch on stones and low branches. Look where the road narrows.

beats.notes: The future world/pickup owner should grant the logical bundle when the collection requirement is satisfied.

beats.title: Fieldwork 2 — return marker cloth

lines.text: That's enough cloth. Ugly, but visible.
Roads don't care about pretty.

beats.notes: Collection hand-in uses existing item-owned/remove-item authoring capabilities.

beats.title: Fieldwork 3 — inspect the outer marker

lines.text: One of the outer markers stopped catching the light last night.
Go look at it. Don't fix anything yet. I want to know whether it fell, broke, or was moved.

beats.notes: Investigation/exploration job. A future authoritative world interaction should set welcome.watch.outer_marker.checked=true after the player inspects the authored marker.

beats.title: Fieldwork 3 — active reminder

lines.text: Look first. Fix later. A changed marker tells you more before you put it back where you think it belongs.

beats.notes: Reminder only.

beats.title: Fieldwork 3 — report the moved marker

lines.text: Turned, not broken.
Wind doesn't usually take the time to point things somewhere else.

beats.notes: The exact world clue is intentionally small. It creates unease without resolving who or what moved the marker.

beats.title: Fieldwork 4 — recover the watch lantern

lines.text: There's an old watch post beyond that marker. I left a shuttered signal lantern there last season.
Bring it back. If something has taken over the post, don't negotiate over my property.

beats.notes: Combined exploration/combat/retrieval job. Exact watch-post geometry and enemy population remain unfrozen.

beats.title: Fieldwork 4 — active reminder

lines.text: Old watch post, beyond the turned marker. Lantern should still be inside if nobody found a use for it first.

beats.notes: Future world content owns placing and granting the lantern item.

beats.title: Fieldwork 4 — return the watch lantern

lines.text: Still works. That's more than I expected.
You too, apparently.

beats.notes: Final fieldwork hand-in. No reward item/currency is invented before the relevant economy/reward owner exists.

beats.title: Fieldwork chain acknowledgement

lines.text: Four jobs out past the gate and you keep coming back through it.
That's a useful habit. Keep it.

beats.notes: Acknowledges the player's increasing field competence without creating a formal tutorial-complete flag.

beats.title: Keeping track of departures

lines.text: I used to count arrivals. After a while you learn to count departures too.
Makes it easier to notice when the numbers don't balance.

beats.notes: Optional thematic line; must never gate progression.

beats.title: Normal road watch filler

lines.text: Quiet road. Best kind.

beats.notes: Low-priority repeatable fallback.

notes: The watchman does not control whether the player may leave Welcome. Gate/travel restrictions are not part of this authoring slice.
The important caravan state is shared with the Traveler and Shopkeeper content through welcome.caravan.important.expected and welcome.caravan.important.late.
The four fieldwork jobs intentionally progress through combat, collection/pickup, investigation, and combined combat/retrieval without tutorial-style exposition.

Kill counts, enemy ContentIds, world locations, pickup counts, and investigation triggers are deliberately not invented here. Their authoritative gameplay owners should set the descriptive completion facts or grant the authored hand-in item when those systems are implemented.

The collection flow uses item.welcome.road_marker_cloth_bundle as one logical hand-in object because the current NPC authoring/test model has boolean item possession rather than quantity-based conditions.
The retrieval flow uses item.welcome.watch_signal_lantern as an authored hand-in reference; it is not yet a runtime ItemDefinition allocation.
No reward item, currency, XP system, or quest manager is introduced by this NPC document.
The road's exact geography remains unfrozen; dialogue avoids naming distances or permanent landmarks that would constrain later map design.
This NPC currently uses the legacy string NPC authoring ID because stable numeric NPC ContentIds are tracked separately in issue #24.
